newsitem.title: USA: Former IRS worker charged with faking deductions.
newsitem.headline: Former IRS worker charged with faking deductions.

text.p: Taxpayers take note on this fateful Tuesday: the IRS is policing its own.

Former part-time Internal Revenue Service employee Janice Waryk was charged with faking $2,825 in charitable donations to a church, a food bank, a seniors center, and the Epilepsy Foundation of America during an audit of her 1990 return.
Waryk, 60, of Strongsville, Ohio, near Cleveland could face up to five years in prison plus a $250,000 fine if found guilty of the federal charges.
The tax agency's own investigators uncovered the allegedly phony deductions.
"We can't comment on the timing" of the charges, said John Siegel, assistant U.S. Attorney in Cleveland, citing the April 15 tax deadline for Americans.
